reference_sql:
SELECT month(order_ts) AS month_no,
       COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
WHERE year(order_ts) = 2025
GROUP BY month(order_ts)
alternatives: SELECT EXTRACT(month FROM order_ts) AS month_no, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1
SELECT date_part('month', order_ts) AS month_no, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE date_part('year', order_ts) = 2025 GROUP BY date_part('month', order_ts)

other_way.sql: SELECT EXTRACT(month FROM order_ts) AS month_no, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1
other_way.tradeoff: Comparing order_ts with two timestamps keeps the column bare, which engines can filter faster than year(order_ts).
